UK Shares Start Week Higher; BP, Shell Decline Amid Lower Oil Prices
Source: MT Newswires (on Yahoo Finance UK) | Monday 2 November 2026, 4:48 pm GMT

Closing levels:
- FTSE 100: 10,761.33 (+31.55, +0.29%)
- FTSE 250: 24,795.85 (+342.49, +1.40%)
- GBP/USD: 1.3415 (+0.0026, +0.19%)
- Gold futures: 3,964.60 (+65.70, +1.69%)

British equities opened the week higher as easing US-Iran tensions drove oil prices lower. President Trump signaled willingness for extended diplomacy, while Tehran confirmed ongoing bilateral communications.
(Search snippet: "British equities started the week higher, with the FTSE 100 up 0.35% on Monday's close, as easing concerns over an immediate military escalation between the US and Iran sent oil prices lower, weighing on energy and commodity stocks.")

UK manufacturing strengthened in October with the S&P Global Manufacturing PMI reaching 52.8 (five-month high), up from 51.9 in September.
S&P Global's Rob Dobson: "Input prices consequently rose to one of the greatest extents in the past four years in October"

BP (BP.L): Down 4.65% after completing the $6 billion sale of a 65% stake in Castrol to Stonepeak, retaining 35% ownership.
Shell (SHEL.L): Down 3.10% following announcement of a long-term exclusive offtake agreement with Green Sky Manara for 150,000 tonnes annual sustainable aviation fuel from a Morocco facility.

Upcoming: Wednesday composite PMI; Thursday car sales, construction PMI, Bank of England rate decision; Friday Lloyds house price index.
